summary: The article examines how the boom in food festivals since around October 1st, 2023 is commercializing traditional cuisines and threatening authentic culinary heritage. It draws on chefs, critics, an anthropologist and a researcher who describe dilution of flavors, uniformity, monoculture farming and pressure to sacrifice quality. It closes with Grandma Mei as an example of resistance and a call for consumers to value authenticity.
one_line: Commercialization of food festivals and traditional dishes is diluting authentic culinary heritage, though figures like Grandma Mei resist and consumers hold responsibility.
key_facts: Grand food festivals began springing up around October 1st, 2023, prompting concern about commercialization of traditional cuisines.

Chef Laila Ansari, who helmed the 'Taste of Heritage' event on September 15, 2023, described culinary heritage as a "palimpsest of stories and practices that define who we are and where we come from."
Edward Thompson, a critic for a prominent food magazine, wrote on November 2, 2023 that festivals are turning into hotbeds for commercialization and making recipes more 'marketable'.
On December 12, 2023, at the 'Global Taste Summit', anthropologist Julia Martin asked whether culinary traditions are being disseminated or diluted when packaged for mass consumption.
Julia Martin argued that tailoring dishes to commercial agendas risks muting the unique flavor profiles that make each dish distinctive.
In a January 18, 2024 interview, Chef Pedro Gomez of Spain lamented that his mother's paella, once a Sunday family gathering staple, has become a fast-food item in tourist restaurants.

Sarah Connors, a sustainable agriculture researcher, said at the 'Future of Farming' conference on February 21, 2024 that demand for 'signature' ingredients leads to monoculture farming that can devastate biodiversity and local agriculture.
Local economies that once thrived on tradition now struggle to compete with mass-produced versions of their own ancestral recipes.
Michelin-starred chef Viktor Chan said at the 'Chefs for Change' summit on March 4, 2024 that chefs face immense pressure to alter recipes for speed and efficiency, often at the cost of quality.
Grandma Mei won the 'Heart of the Community' award on April 2, 2024 for teaching young people to make traditional mooncakes.
The article says responsibility lies with producers and marketers and also with consumers, who must choose between authenticity and a homogenized version.
Examples of culinary heritage cited include the biryani of Hyderabad and the cassoulet of France.
